description: We are a team passionate about robotics, agentic AI, autonomous navigation, and space exploration. Our expertise includes motion planning, simulation, control systems, and software engineering. Our goal is to integrate NASA's planetary data into an intelligent, multi-layer mapping and risk-aware navigation system for future Mars exploration. By combining AI-driven decision-making with autonomous path planning, we aim to support safer and more efficient human exploration of Mars.
summary:
A-STELLAR is a web workspace that brings Mars imagery, terrain-based route planning, scientific context and a conversational planning agent together. Our Jezero Crater demonstration lets a mission team choose destinations, plan an ordered traverse, inspect the evidence behind it and revise the itinerary through conversation.

Planning a future astronaut traverse means connecting science objectives with terrain constraints, travel time and incomplete environmental evidence. A-STELLAR addresses that planning problem by combining NASA resources with specialists for terrain, thermal context, radiation scenarios, geology and rover history. The Mission Planning Agent coordinates available analyses and explains the result; a deterministic Python host computes and checks the A* route.

This demo helps astronauts and ground planners explore a proposed journey, understand its supporting evidence and refine a mission plan in one workspace.
details:
Supporting astronauts on Mars

A future surface mission must connect multiple objectives: reach a science location, visit sites in a required order, account for walking time, and understand which environmental conditions remain uncertain. These decisions involve evidence from different instruments, coordinate systems and time periods.

A-STELLAR explores how a shared workspace could help astronauts and ground planners:

  • Prepare a traverse around terrain constraints and explicit mission priorities.
  • Inspect geological targets and historical rover observations alongside the route.
  • Estimate travel and stop time from stated walking assumptions.
  • Ask why a route was proposed, add a location, or change the visit order.
  • See missing evidence, assessment limitations and source provenance before treating a result as decision support.
  • Export a briefing and retain the relationship between earlier and revised routes.

Mission workspace

Plan a traverse

Choose start and goal coordinates, add up to 16 ordered intermediate visits, and select a terrain objective or mission profile. Advanced controls expose walking speed, stop duration, required analyses and bounded planning resolution. Backend-provided examples make it possible to start with supported DEM locations.

The planner supports regional requests across the configured DEM source, rather than restricting every route to the small initial example window. Actual routes remain subject to data coverage, traversability and search limits.



Explore Mars and its evidence

Use NASA Mars Trek's Viking global imagery and the higher-resolution Jezero HiRISE / CTX / HRSC mosaic for visual context. Available local layers can include DEM coverage and previews, THEMIS day/night previews, geology, science points, rover traverses and rover stops. Visibility and opacity controls let a user inspect these sources independently.

Available spatial layers appear in the map controls. Numerical radiation scenarios appear in the assessment and briefing. Source resolution is recorded alongside the imagery and terrain inputs.

Computed routes are displayed on NASA imagery using the implemented coordinate conversion. Route metadata records the coordinate and pixel-registration status.

Understand the route

The Route view presents distance, walking-time assumptions, ordered legs, actual grid resolution, planning limits and specialist evidence. Profiles include Safest, Fastest, Science priority and Balanced for different mission priorities.

Risk is shown with assessment confidence and evidence coverage. An available-factor partial score excludes missing factors rather than assigning them zero risk. Evidence coverage represents the share of profile weight supported by assessed factors. Blocked or unassessed mission requirements remain visible.

Discuss and revise the plan

The Mission Planner tab supports questions about the stored route and bounded requests to add explicit locations or change their visit order. Informational answers leave the route unchanged. Accepted revisions are computed again by the host, checked, stored, and linked to their parent route.

Agentic mode uses a configured model provider. Deterministic mode keeps terrain planning available without live model calls and offers a narrower explanation workflow. Request status and explicit recovery controls help retrieve completed work without automatically repeating a paid generation request.


Share a mission briefing

The Briefing view organizes known conditions, attention areas and limitations, with technical details available separately. JSON export preserves the route, assessment, source context and unknown values for review.
